acceptanceCriteria: A run with a TMPDIR longer than 128 bytes passes or skips with a clear reason, not an identifier-length failure.
The same tests still pass with a short TMPDIR.
The two failing tests are named in the fix with the identifier source.
body: Context: Go 1.27.1, Darwin arm64, 2026-10-04, origin/main 8a3e3a5b. Two internal/tasks/store tests fail when TMPDIR is long (e.g. /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-.../scratchpad/...) with 'identifier longer than 128 bytes'. They fail identically on main at the BASE 4b10a021 era and pass with a short TMPDIR. Reproduce: GOTOOLCHAIN=local TMPDIR=<path longer than ~100 bytes> go test -count=1 ./internal/tasks/store/. Expected: tests do not depend on TMPDIR length, or skip with a clear reason. Actual: failure from an identifier derived from the temp path exceeding the 128-byte bound. Which two tests and which identifier is not yet recorded; the cause (a path-derived identifier) is an inference from the message.
